sanskrit: yajñā-yajñā vo agnaye girā-girā ca dakṣase | pra-pra vayam amṛtaṁ jātavedasam priyam mitraṁ na śaṁsiṣam ||
english: At every sacrifice and with every hymn we praise you, O Agni, for your wise insight; we extol again and again the immortal Jātavedas as a dear friend.

sanskrit: ūrjo napātaṁ sa hināyam asmayur dāsema havyadātaye | bhuvad vājeṣv avitā bhuvad vṛdha uta trātā tanūnām ||
english: May we serve the Son of Strength who, eager for us, impels us on for the offering of oblations; may he be our protector in prizes of battle, may he be our increaser, and may he be the guardian of our bodies.

sanskrit: vṛṣā hy agne ajaro mahān vibhāsy arciṣā | ajasreṇa sociṣā śosucar chuce sudītibhi su dīdihi ||
english: For thou art the mighty bull, O Agni, the ageless and great, shining with thy flame; blaze with unceasing bright blaze, blazing with clear brightness — shine with fair rays, O pure one.

sanskrit: maho devān yajasi yakṣy ānuṣak tava kratvota daṁsanā | arvācaḥ sīṁ kṛṇuhy agne 'vase rāsva vājota vaṁsva ||
english: Thou worshippest the great gods one after another through thy wisdom and thy wondrous deeds; draw them hither, O Agni, for our protection — bestow upon us strength and win it for us.

sanskrit: yam āpo adrayo vanā garbham ṛtasya piprati | sahasā yo mathito jāyate nṛbhiḥ pṛthivyā adhi sānavi ||
english: He whom the waters, the rocks, and the forests nourish as the embryo of Order — he who is churned into existence with force by men upon the back of the earth.

sanskrit: ā yaḥ paprau bhānunā rodasī ubhe dhūmena dhāvate divi | tiras tamo dadṛśa ūrmyāsv ā śyāvāsv aruṣo vṛṣā śyāvā aruṣo vṛṣā ||
english: He who has filled both worlds of earth and sky with his radiance, and spreads his smoke through heaven; he is seen through the dark nights as the ruddy bull, red in the dark — the ruddy bull, red in the dark.

sanskrit: bṛhadbhir agne arcibhiḥ sukreṇa deva sociṣā | bharadvāje samidhāno yaviṣṭhya revan naḥ śukra dīdihi dyumat pāvaka dīdihi ||
english: With thy great flames and bright divine radiance, O Agni, kindled in the home of Bharadvāja, O youngest one — shine brilliantly for us, O bright one; shine luminously, O purifier.

sanskrit: visvāsāṁ gṛhapatir visām asi tvam agne mānuṣīṇām | satam pūrbhir yaviṣṭha pāhy aṁhasaḥ sameddh āraṁ sataṁ himāḥ sto tṛbhyo ye ca dadati ||
english: Thou art the lord of the household of all human clans, O Agni; guard with a hundred strongholds the one who kindles thee, O youngest, through a hundred winters — guard him from harm along with those praisers who give to thee.

sanskrit: tvaṁ nas citra ūtyā vaso rādhāṁsi codaya | asya rāyas tvam agne rathīr asi vidā gādhaṁ tuce tu naḥ ||
english: With brilliant aid, O shining Vasu, stir up gifts for us; thou, O Agni, art the charioteer of this man's wealth — find us a ford, lead us to the prize.

sanskrit: parṣi tokaṁ tanayam partṛbhiṣ ṭvam adabdhair aprayutvabhiḥ | agne heḻāṁsi daivyā yuyodhi no 'devāni hvarāṁsi ca ||
english: With thy undeceived, unswerving helpers carry our offspring and progeny safely across; ward off from us, O Agni, the divine wrath and the crooked failings of the godless.

sanskrit: ā sakhāyaḥ sabardughāṁ dhenum ajadhvam upa navyasā vacaḥ | sṛjadhvam anapasphurām ||
english: Come, O friends, drive hither the milk-yielding cow with newer words of praise; release her so she shall not kick back.

sanskrit: yā sardhāya mārutāya svabhānave sravo 'mṛtyu dhukṣata | yā mṛḻīke marutāṁ turāṇāṁ yā sumnair evayāvarī ||
english: She who was milked of immortal glory for the bold self-shining troop of Maruts; she who brings the grace of the swift Maruts, she who comes swiftly with their blessings —

sanskrit: bharadvājāyāva dhukṣata dvitā | dhenuṁ ca visvadohasam iṣaṁ ca visvabhojas am ||
english: — she was milked in twain for Bharadvāja: the all-milking cow and the all-nourishing refreshment.

sanskrit: taṁ va indraṁ na sukratuṁ varuṇam iva māyinam | aryamaṇaṁ na mandraṁ sṛprabhojas aṁ viṣṇuṁ na stuṣa ādiśe ||
english: Him I praise, truly pointing the way — Indra like the one of righteous will; Varuṇa like the wizard; Aryaman the gladdening, the lord of rich food; and Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tveṣaṁ sardho na mārutaṁ tuviṣvaṇy anarvāṇam pūṣaṇaṁ saṁ yathā satā | saṁ sahasrā kāriṣac carṣaṇibhyam ām̐ āvir gūḻhā vasū karat suvedā no vasū karat ||
english: Fierce as the Marut host, loudly roaring and unchecked — Pūṣan shall gather a hundred, shall gather a thousand together for the people; he shall reveal hidden riches, shall make them easily known to us.

sanskrit: ā mā pūṣann upa drava saṁsiṣaṁ nu te apikarṇa āghṛṇe | aghā aryo arātayaḥ ||
english: Come running to me, O Pūṣan; I shall now proclaim thy praise close to thine ear, O glowing one — for fierce are the misfortunes of the hostile.

sanskrit: mā kākambīram ud vṛho vanaspatim asastīr vi hi nīnasaḥ | mota sūro aha evā cana grīvā ādadhate veḥ ||
english: Do not uproot the kākambīra tree, the lord of the forest, lest the non-praisers destroy us; and not even the sun on a single day shall place a yoke upon the neck of the flying bird.

sanskrit: dṛter iva te 'vṛkam astu sakhyam | acchidrasya dadhanvataḥ supūrṇasya dadhanvataḥ ||
english: May thy friendship be wolfless, like a leather bag; the friendship of him who holds the unpierceable, the well-filled, the moving one.

sanskrit: paro hi martyair asi samo devair uta sriyā | abhi khyaḥ pūṣan pṛtanāsu nas tvam avā nūnaṁ yathā purā ||
english: For thou art beyond mortals, and equal to the gods in glory; look favourably upon us, O Pūṣan, in battles — protect us now as of old.

sanskrit: vāmī vāmasya dhūtayaḥ praṇītir astu sūnṛtā | devasya vā maruto martyasya vejānasya prayajyavaḥ ||
english: Rich are the impulses of the Bountiful, let the leadership be true and glad; O Maruts, worthy of worship, whether of god or of mortal who is swift to the sacrifice —

sanskrit: sadyas cid yasya carkṛtiḥ pari dyāṁ devo naiti sūryaḥ | tveṣaṁ savo dadhire nāma yajñiyam maruto vṛtrahaṁ savo jyeṣṭhaṁ vṛtrahaṁ savaḥ ||
english: He whose renown the god Sūrya does not pass around the sky even in a day — the Maruts have assumed the fierce, the sacrificially named, Vṛtra-slaying might; the most excellent Vṛtra-slaying might.

sanskrit: sakṛd dha dyaur ajāyata sakṛd bhūmir ajāyata | pṛsnyā dugdhaṁ sakṛt payas tad anyo nānu jāyate ||
english: Heaven was born but once; Earth was born but once; what the dappled cow milked once — that milk — no other is born after it.

sanskrit: stuṣe janaṁ suvrataṁ navyasībhir gīrbhir mitrāvaruṇā sumnayantā | ta ā gamantu ta iha śruvantu sukṣatrāso varuṇo mitro agniḥ ||
english: I praise with newer hymns the folk of good ordinance — Mitra-Varuṇa who bestow favour; may they come hither, may they hear here: the mighty-ruling Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni.

sanskrit: viso-visa īḍyam adhvareṣv adṛptakratum aratiṁ yuvatyoḥ | divaḥ sisum sahasaḥ sūnum agniṁ yajñasya ketum aruṣaṁ yajadhyai ||
english: We worship Agni, lauded at sacrifice after sacrifice, the undaunted Messenger between the two young goddesses — the child of Heaven, the son of Strength, the red banner of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: aruṣasya duhitarā virūpe stṛbhir anyā pipise sūro anyā | mithastūrā vicarantī pāvake manma srutaṁ nakṣata ṛcyamāne ||
english: The two daughters of the ruddy one are of differing forms: one is adorned with stars by the sun, the other with rays; moving together in alternation around the purifier, they have arrived at the famous thought that is being praised.

sanskrit: pra vāyum acchā bṛhatī manīṣā bṛhadrayiṁ visvavāraṁ rathap rām | dyutadyāmā niyutaḥ patyamānaḥ kaviḥ kavim iyakṣasi prayajyo ||
english: With great thought toward Vāyu, laden with vast treasure, containing all goods, filling the chariot — thou who art the lord of the shining path, the lord of the harnessed ones, the sage seeks the sage, O thou worthy of worship.

sanskrit: sa me vapus chadayad asvinor yo ratho virukmān manasā yujānaḥ | yena narā nāsatyeṣayadhyai vartir yāthas tanayāya tmane ca ||
english: May the gleaming chariot of the Aśvins, which is yoked by thought, be pleasing to my body; with which, O heroes, ye travel the path for the Nāsatyas to proceed, for offspring and for self.

sanskrit: parjanyavātā vṛṣabhā pṛthivyāḥ purīṣāṇi jinvatam apyāni | satyasrutaḥ kavayo yasya gīrbhir jagataḥ sthātar jagad ā kṛṇudhvam ||
english: O Parjanya and Vāta, bulls of earth, quicken the waters that fill the moisture; ye true-hearing sages — with whose hymns ye, O Stayer of the world, make the world move.

sanskrit: pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ sarasvatī vīrapatnī dhiyaṁ dhāt | gnābhir acchidraṁ saraṇaṁ sajoṣā durādharṣaṁ gṛṇate sarma yaṁsat ||
english: The brilliant Sarasvatī, the wondrous-lived maiden, the wife of heroes, shall bestow thought; together with the divine wives she shall, with unbroken shelter, grant impregnable refuge to the singer.

sanskrit: pathas-pathaḥ paripatiṁ vacasyā kāmena kṛto abhy ānaḻ arkam | sa no rāsac churudhas candrāgrā dhiyaṁ-dhiyaṁ sīṣadhāti pra pūṣā ||
english: With desire wrought in praise the guardian of every path has approached the hymn; may Pūṣan bestow upon us gifts that grant brilliant plenty, and accomplish thought after thought for us.

sanskrit: prathamabhājaṁ yasasaṁ vayodhāṁ supāṇiṁ devaṁ sugabhastim ṛbhvam | hotā yakṣad yajataṁ pastyānām agnis tvaṣṭāraṁ suhavaṁ vibhāvā ||
english: May Agni the far-shining Hotṛ, the good invocable one, worship the adorable Tvaṣṭṛ of the household — first partaker, glorious, life-giving, fair-handed, the divine and brilliant-armed great craftsman.

sanskrit: bhuvanasya pitaraṁ gīrbhir ābhī rudraṁ divā vardhayā rudram aktau | bṛhantam ṛṣvam ajaraṁ suṣumnam ṛdhag ghuvema kavin eṣitāsaḥ ||
english: With these hymns strengthen Rudra, the father of the world, by day, strengthen Rudra at night; the great, the high, the ageless, the benevolent — we shall call him apart, sent forth by the sage.

sanskrit: ā yuvānaḥ kavayo yajñiyāso maruto ganta gṛṇato varasyām | acitraṁ cid dhi jinvathā vṛdhanta itthā nakṣanto naro aṅgirasvat ||
english: Come hither, O young, wise, sacrifice-worthy Maruts, to the desire of the praiser; for ye quicken even the undistinguished to grow, O heroes, truly approaching like Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: pra vīrāya pra tavase turāyājā yūtheva pasurakṣir astam | sa pispṛsati tanvi srutasya stṛbhir na nākaṁ vacanasya vipaḥ ||
english: The herd-keeper who guards the cattle goes forth home for the hero, for the mighty, for the swift one; he touches with his body the heaven of the famous one, like stars in the firmament of speech.

sanskrit: yo rajāṁsi vimame pārthivāni tris cid viṣṇur manave bādhitāya | tasya te sarmann upadad yamāne rāyā madema tanvā tanā ca ||
english: Viṣṇu who measured out the earthly realms in three steps for oppressed Manu — in thy protection, O Viṣṇu, while it is being bestowed, may we rejoice with wealth, with body, and with offspring.

sanskrit: tan no 'hir budhnyaḥ adbhir arkais tat parvatas tat savitā cano dhāt | tad oṣadhībhir abhi rātiṣāco bhagaḥ puraṁdhir jinvatu pra rāye ||
english: May Ahi Budhnya bestow that on us with waters and hymns; may the Mountain and Savitṛ bestow that favour; may Bhaga the full-bestowing, aided by plants, quicken that for our prosperity.

sanskrit: nu no rayiṁ rathyaṁ carṣaṇiprām puruvīram maha ṛtasya gopām | kṣayaṁ dātājaram yena janān spṛdho adevīr abhi ca kramāma visa ādevīr abhy asnāvāma ||
english: Now bestow upon us wealth borne on chariots, filling the folk, rich in heroes, guardian of the great Order — an imperishable dwelling whereby we may stride over the godless rivalries of people, may we overcome the godless hosts.

sanskrit: huve vo devīm aditiṁ namobhir mṛḻīkāya varuṇam mitram agnim | abhikṣadām aryamaṇaṁ susevaṁ trātṝn devān savitāram bhagaṁ ca ||
english: I call with obeisances divine Aditi for grace; Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni; and Aryaman the bestower, the well-kind, the protecting gods Savitṛ and Bhaga.

sanskrit: sujyotiṣaḥ sūrya dakṣapitṝn anāgāstve sumaho vīhi devān | dvijanmāno ya ṛtasāpaḥ satyāḥ svarvanto yajatā agnijihvāḥ ||
english: O Sūrya of good light, O great one, announce the gods of good skill who are fathers of wisdom, who are guiltless — the twice-born, the true attainers of Order, the celestial, the adorable, the Agni-tongued.

sanskrit: uta dyāvāpṛthivī kṣatram uru bṛhad rodasī saraṇaṁ suṣumne | mahas karatho varivo yathā no 'sme kṣayāya dhiṣaṇe anehaḥ ||
english: May Heaven and Earth, the two worlds of great dominion, grant us wide and large refuge in their benevolence; may the two wise goddesses, being blameless, make abundance for our dwelling.

sanskrit: ā no rudrasya sūnavo namantām adyā hūtāso vasavo 'dhṛṣṭāḥ | yad īm arbhe mahati vā hitāso bādhe maruto ahvāma devān ||
english: May the sons of Rudra bow to us today when called — the Vasus, the resistless ones; for when in small or great need, pressed hard, we have called the gods, the Maruts.

sanskrit: mimyakṣa yeṣu rodasī nu devī siṣakti pūṣā abhyardhayajvā | srutvā havam maruto yad dha yātha bhūmā rejante adhvani pravikṭe ||
english: In whom both divine worlds are fixed, whom the half-sacrificer Pūṣan follows closely — when on hearing the call the Maruts come along the separated path, the vast spaces shake.

sanskrit: abhi tyaṁ vīraṁ girvaṇasam arcendram brahmaṇā jaritar navena | sravad id havam upa ca stavāno rāsad vājām upa maho gṛṇānaḥ ||
english: With a new prayer praise Indra the hero who is fond of hymns, O singer; let him hear the call, being praised, and may he bestow prizes when invoked with a great invocation.

sanskrit: omānam āpo mānuṣīr amṛktaṁ dhāta tokāya tanayāya saṁ yoḥ | yūyaṁ hi ṣṭhā bhiṣajo mātṛtamā viśvasya sthātur jagato janitrīḥ ||
english: O Waters that belong to men, pour out an inviolate, health-giving boon for offspring and posterity; for ye are the greatest physicians and greatest mothers, the source of all that stands still and all that moves.

sanskrit: ā no devaḥ savitā trāyamāṇo hiraṇyapāṇir yajato jagamyāt | yo datravām̐ uṣaso na pratīkaṁ vyūrṇute dāsuse vāryāṇi ||
english: May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, the adorable, protecting us, come hither; he who, like the face of Dawn, generous, unveils desirable gifts for the worshipper.

sanskrit: uta tvaṁ sūno sahaso no adyā devām asminn adhvare vavṛtyāḥ | syām ahaṁ te sadam id rātau tava syām agne 'vasā suvīraḥ ||
english: And thou, O Son of Strength, mayst thou today turn the gods toward us at this sacrifice; may I ever dwell in thy bounty — may I, O Agni, dwell under thy protection with good heroes.

sanskrit: uta tyā me havam ā jagmyātaṁ nāsatyā dhībhir yuvam aṅga viprā | atriṁ na mahas tamaso 'mumukta ṁ tūrvataṁ narā duritād abhīke ||
english: And may those two Nāsatyas, O wise ones, truly come with their thoughts to my call; as ye delivered Atri from the great darkness, hasten, O heroes, to free him from mis-adventure.

sanskrit: te no rāyo dyumato vājav ato dātāro bhūta nṛvataḥ purukṣoḥ | dasasyanto divyāḥ pārthivāso gojātā apyā mṛḻatā ca devāḥ ||
english: Be givers to us of wealth that is bright, prize-winning, rich in men and abundance; ye divine and earthly gods, born of cattle and of waters, ministering and gracious — be gracious to us.

sanskrit: te no rudraḥ sarasvatī sajoṣā mīḻhuṣmanto viṣṇur mṛḻantu vāyuḥ | ṛbhukṣā vājo daivyo vidhātā parjanyāvātā pipyatām iṣaṁ naḥ ||
english: May Rudra, Sarasvatī, the bountiful Viṣṇu, and Vāyu — together — be gracious to us; may Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, the divine dispenser, Parjanya, and Vāta swell our refreshment.

sanskrit: uta sya devaḥ savitā bhago no 'pāṁ napād avatu dānu papriḥ | tvaṣṭā devebhir janibhiḥ sajoṣā dyaur devebhiḥ pṛthivī samudraiḥ ||
english: And may the god Savitṛ, may Bhaga, may Apāṁ Napāt who fills with moisture, protect us; Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine birth-goddesses, and Heaven with the gods, and Earth with the oceans.

sanskrit: uta no 'hir budhnyaḥ sṛṇotv aja ekapāt pṛthivī samudraḥ | viśve devā ṛtāvṛdho huvānāḥ stutā mantrāḥ kavisastā avantu ||
english: And may Ahi Budhnya hear us, and Aja Ekapād, the Earth, and the Ocean; let all the gods who increase Order when called upon protect us — let the praised mantras, proclaimed by the sage, protect us.

sanskrit: evā napāto mama tasya dhībhir bharadvājā abhy arcanty arkaiḥ | gnā hutāso vasavo 'dhṛṣṭā viśve stutāso bhūtā yajatrāḥ ||
english: So the Bharadvājas, those worthy sons, worship him with their thoughts and hymns; the divine consorts invoked, the resistless Vasus, all the adorable ones — be praised and honoured.

sanskrit: ud u tyac cakṣur mahi mitrayor ām eti priyaṁ varuṇayor adabdham | ṛtasya suci darśatam anīkaṁ rukmo na diva uditā vy adyaut ||
english: Up there rises that great eye of the two Mitras, the beloved and undeceived eye of the two Varuṇas; the pure, visible face of Order blazed forth like a golden ornament at dawn.

sanskrit: veda yas trīṇi vidathāny eṣāṁ devānāṁ janma sanutar ā ca vipraḥ | ṛju marteṣu vṛjinā ca pasyan abhi caṣṭe sūro aryam evān ||
english: The wise one who knows the three assemblies of these gods and their birth from of old — beholding what is straight and what is crooked among mortals, the sun surveys even the paths of Aryaman.

sanskrit: stuṣa u vo maha ṛtasya gopān aditim mitraṁ varuṇaṁ sujātān | aryamaṇam bhagam adabdhadhītīn acchā voce sadhanyaḥ pāvakān ||
english: I praise the great guardians of Order — Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa well-born; Aryaman, Bhaga, they of undeluded wisdom — I address them together, the purifiers.

sanskrit: risādasaḥ satpatīmr adabdhān maho rājñaḥ suvasanasya dātṝn | yūnaḥ sukṣatrān kṣayato divo nṝn ādityān yāmy aditiṁ duvoyuḥ ||
english: Desiring to serve, I go to the Ādityas — destroyers of enemies, the true lords, undeceived, great kings, givers of fine clothing, the young and mighty rulers of heaven, and to Aditi.

sanskrit: dyau3ṣ pitaḥ pṛthivi mātar adhrug agne bhrātar vasavo mṛḻatā naḥ | visva ādityā adite sajoṣā asmabhyaṁ sarma bahulaṁ vi yanta ||
english: O Father Heaven, O blameless Mother Earth, O Agni our brother, O Vasus — be gracious to us; all ye Ādityas, O Aditi together, spread out broad shelter for us.

sanskrit: mā no vṛkāya vṛkye samasmā aghāyate rīradhatā yajatrāḥ | yūyaṁ hi ṣṭhā rathyo nas tanūnāṁ yūyaṁ dakṣasya vacaso babhūva ||
english: Do not deliver us to the wolf, to the she-wolf — to the equally matched evil-doer, O adorable ones; for ye are the charioteers of our bodies, ye have become the lords of understanding and speech.

sanskrit: mā va eno anyakṛtam bhujema mā tat karma vasavo yac cayadhve | viśvasya hi kṣayatha viśvadevāḥ svayaṁ ripus tanvaṁ rīriṣīṣṭa ||
english: May we not suffer the sin done by another; may we not perform that deed which ye, O Vasus, will avenge; for ye, O All-Gods, rule over all — let the deceiver harm his own body.

sanskrit: nama id ugraṁ nama ā vivāse namo dādhāra pṛthivīm uta dyām | namo devebhyo nama īsa eṣāṁ kṛtaṁ cid eno namasā vivāse ||
english: With reverence I seek the mighty reverence; reverence has upheld the earth and heaven; reverence to the gods, reverence to the lord of these — even sin already done I seek to purify with reverence.

sanskrit: ṛtasya vo rathyaḥ pūtadakṣān ṛtasya pastyasado adabdhān | tām̐ ā namobhir urucakṣaso nṝn visvān va ā name maho yajatrāḥ ||
english: The charioteers of Order, with purified skill; the undeceived, seated in the dwelling of Order — to those far-seeing heroes I bow with obeisances; I bow down before all of you great adorable ones.

sanskrit: te hi sreṣṭhavarcasas ta u nas tiro visvāni duritā nayanti | sukṣatrāso varuṇo mitro agnir ṛtadhītayo vakmarāja satyāḥ ||
english: For they are of supreme splendour, and they lead us across all evils — the mighty-ruling Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, who think on Order, truly spoken and truthful.

sanskrit: te na indraḥ pṛthivī kṣāma vardhan pūṣā bhago aditiḥ pañca janāḥ | suśarmāṇaḥ svavasan sunīthā bhavantu naḥ sutrātrāsaḥ sugopāḥ ||
english: May they — Indra, Earth, the territory, Pūṣan, Bhaga, Aditi, the five peoples — granting good shelter, good dwelling, and good guidance, be for us good protectors and good guardians.

sanskrit: nū sadmānaṁ divyaṁ naṁsi devā bhāradvājaḥ sumatiṁ yāti hotā | āsānebhir yajamāno miyedhair devānāṁ janma vasūyur vavanda ||
english: Now the gods greet the heavenly dwelling; the Bharadvāja priest, the Hotṛ, proceeds to the divine benevolence; with the sacrificial seatings and offerings the worshipper, desiring wealth, has praised the birth of the gods.

sanskrit: apa tyaṁ vṛjinaṁ ripuṁ stenam agne durādhyam | daviṣṭham asya satpate kṛdhī sugam ||
english: Drive away, O Agni, that crooked enemy, the thief who is hard to overcome; make easy for us, O Lord of Truth, the most distant path.

sanskrit: grāvāṇaḥ soma no hi kaṁ sakhitvanāya vāvasuḥ | jahī ny a1triṇam paṇiṁ vṛko hi ṣaḥ ||
english: O pressing stones, O Soma, ye have called out for our friendship; strike down the devouring Paṇi — for he is a wolf.

sanskrit: yūyaṁ hi ṣṭhā sudānava indrajyeṣṭhā abhidyavaḥ | kartā no adhvann ā sugaṁ gopā amā ||
english: For ye are the good givers, those for whom Indra is greatest, who shine against heaven; make for us on the path an easy way, O house-dwelling guardians.

sanskrit: api panthām aganmahi svastigām anehasam | yena visvāḥ pari dviṣo vṛṇakti vindate vasu ||
english: May we find the path that leads to welfare, that is blameless, whereby one wards off all foes and discovers treasure.

sanskrit: na tad divā na pṛthivyānu manye na yajñena nota samībhir ābhiḥ | ubjantu taṁ subhva1ḥ parvatāso ni hīyatām atiyājasya yaṣṭā ||
english: I do not approve of that — neither by sky nor by earth, neither by sacrifice nor by these exertions; may the mighty mountains press down the one who sacrifices too extravagantly — let the performer of excess-sacrifice fall low.

sanskrit: ati vā yo maruto manyate no brahma vā yaḥ kriyamāṇaṁ ninitsāt | tapūṁṣi tasmai vṛjināni santu brahmadviṣam abhi taṁ socatu dyauḥ ||
english: He who thinks to surpass us, O Maruts, or who wishes to blame the prayer being composed — let sharp afflictions and crooked misfortunes be his lot; let Heaven blaze down upon that hater of prayer.

sanskrit: kim aṅga tvā brahmaṇaḥ soma gopāṁ kim aṅga tvāhur abhisastipāṁ naḥ | kim aṅga naḥ pasya si nidyamānān brahmadviṣe tapusiṁ hetim asya ||
english: O Soma, guardian of the prayer — what indeed do they call thee? And the protector of us from calumny — what indeed? Look upon us as we are being reviled and hurl thy scorching weapon at the hater of prayer.

sanskrit: avantu mām uṣaso jāyamānā avantu mā sindhavaḥ pinvamānāḥ | avantu mā parvatāso dhruvāso 'vantu mā pitaro devahūtau ||
english: May the Dawns as they rise protect me; may the swelling Rivers protect me; may the firm Mountains protect me; may the Fathers protect me when the gods are invoked.

sanskrit: visvadānīṁ sumanasaḥ syāma pasyema nu sūryam uccarantam | tathā karad vasupatiḥ vasūnāṁ devām̐ ohāno 'vasāgamiṣṭhaḥ ||
english: May we always be of good mind; may we behold the sun rising; so may the lord of good things among goods do it — the most easily approached, driving the gods.

sanskrit: indro nediṣṭham avasāgamiṣṭhaḥ sarasvatī sindhubhiḥ pinvamānā | parjanyo na oṣadhībhir mayobhur agniḥ suśaṁsaḥ suhavaḥ piteva ||
english: Indra is the nearest and most easily approached for protection; Sarasvatī swelling with rivers; Parjanya bringing delight with his plants; Agni of fair praise, easy to invoke, like a father.

sanskrit: visve devāsa ā gata sṛṇutā ma imaṁ havam | edam barhir ni ṣīdata ||
english: Come, all ye gods; hear my call; sit down on this sacred grass.

sanskrit: yo vo devā ghṛtasnunā havyena pratibhūṣati | taṁ visva upa gacchatha ||
english: He who adorns you, O gods, with the oblation rich in ghee — all of you, come to him.

sanskrit: upa naḥ sūnavo giraḥ sṛṇvanty amṛtasya ye | sumṛḻīkā bhavantu naḥ ||
english: May the sons who are immortal hear our hymns — may they be gracious to us.

sanskrit: visve devā ṛtāvṛdha ṛtubhir havanasrutaḥ | juṣantāṁ yujyam payaḥ ||
english: All ye gods who increase Order, who hear the call at the proper seasons — enjoy the meet milk-offering.

sanskrit: stotram indro marudgaṇas tvaṣṭṛmān mitro aryamā | imā havyā juṣanta naḥ ||
english: May Indra, the host of Maruts, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, and Aryaman enjoy this praise and these oblations of ours.

sanskrit: imaṁ no agne adhvaraṁ hotar vayunaso yaja | cikitvān daivyaṁ janam ||
english: Sacrifice at this our rite, O Agni, O Hotṛ, knowing the ways; be discerning of the divine folk.

sanskrit: visve devāḥ sṛṇutemaṁ havam me ye antarikṣe ya upa dyavi ṣṭha | ye agnijihvā uta vā yajatrā āsadyāsmin barhiṣi mādayadhvam ||
english: All ye gods, hear this my call — ye who are in the mid-air and ye who dwell up in heaven; ye whose tongue is Agni, and ye who are adorable — sit down upon this sacred grass and rejoice.

sanskrit: visve devā mama sṛṇvantu yajñiyā ubhe rodasī apāṁ napāc ca manma | mā vo vacāṁsi paricakṣyāṇi vocaṁ sumneṣv id vo antamā madema ||
english: May all the sacrifice-worthy gods hear my thought, both worlds, and Apāṁ Napāt; may I not speak words that should be concealed from you — may we rejoice in your blessings, the most intimate of yours.

sanskrit: ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyā divo jajñire apāṁ sadhasthe | te asmabhyam iṣaye visvam āyuḥ kṣapa usrā varivasyantu devāḥ ||
english: Whatever great ones here on earth, who hold the serpent's magic, were born from heaven and from the seat of the waters — may those gods grant us full life-span for sustenance through nights and dawns.

sanskrit: agnīparjanyāv avataṁ dhiyam me 'smin have suhavā suṣṭutiṁ naḥ | iḻām anyo janayad garbham anyaḥ prajāvatīr iṣa ā dhattam asme ||
english: O Agni and Parjanya, aid my thought in this invocation — easy to call, our good praise; one of you engenders Iḻā and one engenders the embryo — bestow upon us refreshment rich in progeny.

sanskrit: stīrṇe barhiṣi samidhāne agnau sūktena mahā namasā vivāse | asmin no adya vidathe yajatrā visve devā haviṣi mādayadhvam ||
english: With the sacred grass strewn and Agni kindled, with the well-chanted hymn and great reverence I seek you; at this our assembly today, O adorable All-Gods, rejoice in the oblations.

sanskrit: vayam u tvā pathas pate rathaṁ na vājasātaye | dhiye pūṣann ayujmahi ||
english: We have yoked thee, O lord of the path, O Pūṣan, like a chariot for the winning of prizes, for our thought.

sanskrit: abhi no naryaṁ vasu vīram prayatadakṣiṇam | vāmaṁ gṛhapatiṁ naya ||
english: Lead us to the manly wealth, to the hero with outstretched right hand — the beautiful lord of the house.

sanskrit: aditsantaṁ cid āghṛṇe pūṣan dānāya codaya | paṇes cid vi mradā manaḥ ||
english: Even him who is unwilling to give, O glowing Pūṣan, spur to generosity; soften even the mind of the miser.

sanskrit: vi patho vājasātaye cinuhi vi mṛdho jahi | sādhantām ugra no dhiyaḥ ||
english: Clear the paths for the winning of prizes; scatter and slay the adversaries; may our thoughts, O fierce one, be made effective.

sanskrit: pari tṛndhi paṇīnām ārayā hṛdayā kave | athem asmabhyaṁ randhaya ||
english: Pierce through the hearts of the Paṇis with thy goad, O sage; and then subject them to us.

sanskrit: vi pūṣann ārayā tuda paṇer iccha hṛdi priyam | athem asmabhyaṁ randhaya ||
english: O Pūṣan, pierce with thy goad and seek out what is dear in the heart of the Paṇi; and then subject him to us.

sanskrit: ā rikha kikirā kṛṇu paṇīnāṁ hṛdayā kave | athem asmabhyaṁ randhaya ||
english: Scratch and scrape, make crumbling the hearts of the Paṇis, O sage; and then subject them to us.

sanskrit: yām pūṣan brahmacodanīm ārām bibharṣy āghṛṇe | tayā samasya hṛday am ā rikha kikirā kṛṇu ||
english: The goad that is the impeller of prayer, O glowing Pūṣan, which thou bearest — with that scratch the heart of the churlish one and make it crumbling.

sanskrit: yā te aṣṭrā goopasāghṛṇe pasusādhanī | tasyās te sumnam īmahe ||
english: The driving rod that fastens cattle, O glowing one, the subduer of beasts — we beg for the favour of that one of thine.

sanskrit: uta no goṣaṇiṁ dhiyam asvasāṁ vājasām uta | nṛvat kṛṇuhi vītaye ||
english: Also grant us thought that wins cattle, that wins horses, that wins prizes — make it rich in men for the feast.

sanskrit: sam pūṣan viduṣā naya yo añjasānusāsati | ya evedam iti bravat ||
english: Lead us together, O Pūṣan, with the one who knows, who teaches us straightforwardly, who says 'This is exactly the way.'

sanskrit: sam u pūṣṇā gamemahi yo gṛhām abhisāsati | ima eveti ca bravat ||
english: May we go together with Pūṣan and with him who points out the homesteads and says 'These are the ones right here.'

sanskrit: pūṣṇas cakraṁ na riṣyati na koso 'va padyate | no asya vyathate paviḥ ||
english: The wheel of Pūṣan is not harmed; the basket does not fall; his wheel-rim does not wobble.

sanskrit: yo asmai haviṣāvidhan na tam pūṣāpi mṛṣyate | prathamo vindate vasu ||
english: He who has served him with an oblation — Pūṣan does not neglect him; he is first to find wealth.

sanskrit: pūṣā gā anv etu naḥ pūṣā rakṣatv arvataḥ | pūṣā vājaṁ sanotu naḥ ||
english: May Pūṣan follow after our cattle; may Pūṣan protect our steeds; may Pūṣan win prizes for us.

sanskrit: pūṣann anu pra gā ihi yajamānasya sunvataḥ | asmākaṁ stuvat ām uta ||
english: O Pūṣan, go forward after the cattle of the pressing worshipper and also of our praisers.

sanskrit: mākir nesan mākīṁ riṣan mākīṁ saṁ sāri kevaṭe | athāriṣṭābhir ā gahi ||
english: May none be lost, may none come to harm, may none fall into a pit; come hither with all unhurt.

sanskrit: sṛṇvantam pūṣaṇaṁ vayam iryam anaṣṭavedasam | īsānaṁ rāya īmahe ||
english: We beg of Pūṣan the listener, the movable one who has not lost his wealth — we beg of the lord of riches.

sanskrit: pūṣan tava vrate vayaṁ na riṣyema kadā cana | stotāras ta iha smasi ||
english: In thy ordinance, O Pūṣan, may we never suffer harm; here we are, thy praisers.

sanskrit: pari pūṣā parastād dhastaṁ dadhātu dakṣiṇam | punar no naṣṭam ājatu ||
english: May Pūṣan place his right hand behind us; may he drive back to us what is lost.

sanskrit: ehi vāṁ vimuco napād āghṛṇe saṁ sacāvahai | rathīr ṛtasya no bhava ||
english: Come, O descendant of Vimuco, O glowing Pūṣan; let us be together — be the charioteer of Order for us.

sanskrit: rathītamaṁ kapardinam īsānaṁ rādhaso mahaḥ | rāyaḥ sakhāyam īmahe ||
english: We pray for the friendship of the most chariot-worthy Kapardī, the lord of great bounty — the friend of wealth.

sanskrit: rāyo dhārāsy āghṛṇe vaso rāsir ajāsva | dhīvato-dhīvataḥ sakhā ||
english: Thou art a stream of riches, O glowing Vasu, a heap of wealth, the goat-horsed one — the friend of the wise one after wise one.

sanskrit: pūṣaṇaṁ nv a1jāsvam upa stoṣāma vājinam | svasur yo jāra ucyate ||
english: Now let us praise Pūṣan the goat-horse, the prize-winning, who is called the lover of his sister.

sanskrit: mātur didhiṣum abravaṁ svasur jāraḥ sṛṇotu naḥ | bhrātendrasya sakhā mama ||
english: I spoke of the suitor of the mother — may the lover of the sister hear us: the brother of Indra and my companion.

sanskrit: ājāsaḥ pūṣaṇaṁ rathe nisṛmbhās te janasriyam | devaṁ vahantu bibhrataḥ ||
english: The goats, unharnessed on his chariot, bearing him, carry Pūṣan the glorious among men, the divine.

sanskrit: ya enam ādidesati karambhād iti pūṣaṇam | na tena deva ādiśe ||
english: He who points out this Pūṣan as 'From Karambha' — with that one, O god, I do not agree.

sanskrit: uta ghā sa rathītamaḥ sakhyā satpatir yujā | indro vṛtrāṇi jighnate ||
english: Yet truly that most chariot-worthy one, as a friend and ally — the true lord — Indra, smites the Vṛtras.

sanskrit: utādaḥ paruṣe gavi sūras cakraṁ hiraṇyayam | ny airayad rathītamaḥ ||
english: And there, in the dappled cow, the sun drove down his golden wheel — the most chariot-worthy one.

sanskrit: yad adya tvā puruṣṭuta bravāma dasra mantumaḥ | tat su no manma sādhaya ||
english: What we say to thee today, O much-praised, wonderful, thoughtful one — accomplish that thought well for us.

sanskrit: imaṁ ca no gaveṣaṇaṁ sātaye sīṣadho gaṇam | ārāt pūṣann asi srutaḥ ||
english: And make this cow-seeking host of ours succeed for the prize; thou art heard of from afar, O Pūṣan.

sanskrit: ā te svastim īmaha āreaghām upāvasum | adyā ca sarvatātaye svaś ca sarvatātaye ||
english: We beg of thee a welfare that is free from evil and near at hand — for completeness today and for completeness tomorrow.

sanskrit: indrā nu pūṣaṇā vayaṁ sakhyāya svastaye | huvema vājasātaye ||
english: Now let us call upon Indra and Pūṣan together for friendship, for welfare, for the winning of prizes.

sanskrit: somam anya upāsadat pātave camvoḥ sutam | karambham anya icchati ||
english: One of them (Indra) has sat near the Soma pressed in the bowls to drink; the other (Pūṣan) seeks the porridge (karambha).

sanskrit: ajā anyasya vahnayo harī anyasya sambhṛtā | tābhyāṁ vṛtrāṇi jighnate ||
english: Goats are the steeds of one, the two bays are harnessed for the other; with these two they smite the Vṛtras.

sanskrit: yad indro anayad rito mahīr apo vṛṣantamaḥ | tatra pūṣābhavat sacā ||
english: When Indra the most showery one drove the great waters in proper order, there Pūṣan was with him as a companion.

sanskrit: tām pūṣṇaḥ sumatiṁ vayaṁ vṛkṣasya pra vayām iva | indrasya cā rabhāmahe ||
english: That benevolence of Pūṣan and of Indra we lay hold of, like a branch of a tree.

sanskrit: ut pūṣaṇaṁ yuvāmahe 'bhīsūmr iva sārathiḥ | mahyā indraṁ svastaye ||
english: We lift up Pūṣan like reins held by a charioteer, and Indra for our welfare and greatness.
